history.summary: Kempe Gowda I, founder of Bengaluru, is said to have found a large rock resembling Ganesha near Bugle Rock in Basavanagudi and had sculptors carve it into an 18-ft tall, 16-ft wide monolithic idol; many devotees regard it as swayambhu (self-formed). The temple was built around the idol in the 16th century and renovated in the 1970s to handle crowds. The daily 'benne (butter) alankara' — the idol coated with layers of butter — is a distinctive living ritual.

name: Shree Dodda Ganapathi Temple
town_description: Bengaluru, capital of Karnataka, is a major Indian metropolis known for its tech industry and colonial-era garden heritage. Basavanagudi is one of the city's oldest neighbourhoods, home to the 16th-century Bull Temple, Bugle Rock Park, and Kempe Gowda-era landmarks.

travel.railway: Krantivira Sangolli Rayanna (KSR) Bengaluru city station (~5 km); Lalbagh metro station (~1.3 km)
travel.road: Bull Temple Road, Basavanagudi; city buses and autos readily available

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early mornings or evenings to avoid crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 5:30 PM-9:00 PM daily (one source gives the midday close as 12:00 PM; verify)
